 ORDER

This second bail application has been filed by applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for grant of bail in connection with Crime No.401 of 2023 registered at Police Station Kailaras, District Morena (M.P.), for offence punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376 of IPC and Section 5/6 of POCSO Act.
The applicant is in judicial custody since 22.09.2023.
First bail application of applicant was dismissed as withdrawn by this Court vide order dated 12.12.2023 passed in MCRC No.54330/2023.
Thereafter, victim (PW-1) and her sister (PW-2) have been examined before the learned trial Court.
As per the prosecution case, mother of the victim reported to Police Station Kailaras, District Morena that her daughter aged 14 years is missing from 15.09.2023.
She suspects that Vikas Kushwah has enticed and taken her daughter.
On such allegations, Police Station Kailaras registered FIR at Crime No.401 of 2024 for offence punishable under Sections 363 of IPC.

sentences.text: Victim stated that Vikas Kushwah enticed and taken her to Gwalior and Pune.
They stayed in a room at Pune.
Vikas committed rape on her.
She returned home on 21.09.2023.
Applicant was arrested on 22.09.2023.
He is in custody ever since.
Victim was sent for examination of DNA report.
DNA extracted from the undergarment of victim matched with the DNA sample of the accused.
Thereafter, Prosecution for offence punishable under Sections 366 and 376 of IPC and Section 5/6 of POCSO Act was added.
On completion of investigation, Final Report was submitted on 09.10.2023.
The trial is underway.

Learned Counsel for the applicant, in addition to the grounds mentioned in the application, submits that applicant has been falsely implicated in this matter under the pressure of family members of the victim.
It is a case of romantic relationship between two young persons.
Victim was major at the time of incident.
She left her parental home at her own.
Learned counsel referring to the statements of PW-1 and PW-2 submits that both of them have not supported the prosecution and denied the allegation against the applicant.
Victim has stated that her age was 19 years at the time of incident.
Learned counsel further submits that applicant is Labourer by profession and is aged around 22 years.
He is sole bread earner of the family, therefore, there is no likelihood of absconsion leaving his family and home.
No criminal antecedent is reported against the applicant.
No further custodial interrogation is needed.
There is no likelihood of tampering with evidence.
Jail incarceration is causing hardship to the applicant.
Therefore, applicant may be extended the benefit of bail.
P er contra, learned Counsel for the State opposes the bail application on the ground of gravity of alleged offence.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
Considering the arguments advanced by both the parties and overall circumstances o f the case, but without commenting on merits of the case, this Court is inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Thus, the application is allowed.
